summary: d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem are allocated with 'nelements' entries but the constructor fills 'ntypes' of them (and sinner/dinner at index i instead of i-1), so any run with more atom types than SNAP elements writes past the end of the host mirrors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:76-79 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_radelem,"...",nelements); ... d_wjelem ... d_sinnerelem ... d_dinnerelem' followed by :96-103 'for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { h_radelem(i-1) = radelem[i]; h_wjelem(i-1) = wjelem[i]; if (switchinnerflag){ h_sinnerelem(i) = sinnerelem[i]; h_dinnerelem(i) = dinnerelem[i]; } }'. In ComputeSNAGrid radelem/wjelem are per-TYPE arrays of size ntypes+1 (src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:62-72) while nelements defaults to 1 and is only changed by the 'chem' keyword (:57 and :115-119). Contrast the correct pattern in src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:484-492 'for (int ielem = 0; ielem < nelements; ielem++) { h_radelem(ielem) = radelem[ielem]; ... }'. The identical code is in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:95-102.
failure_scenario: 'compute g all sna/grid/kk grid 10 10 10 4.0 0.99363 6 0.5 0.7 1.0 1.0' with 2 atom types and no 'chem' keyword: nelements==1, so h_radelem(1) and h_wjelem(1) write one element past a 1-element host allocation -> heap corruption (an immediate abort under KOKKOS_ENABLE_DEBUG_BOUNDS_CHECK).
suggested_fix: Size these views with atom->ntypes (matching the 1-based per-type arrays they mirror) and use consistent i-1 indexing for all four, or switch to genuinely per-element arrays as pair snap/kk does.

summary: The PreUi kernels look up 'type(iatom)' where iatom is a grid-point index, not an atom index, giving a wrong (or out-of-bounds) element for the central site.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:516-524 'const int iatom = iatom_mod + iatom_div * vector_length; if (iatom >= chunk_size) return; int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);' -- iatom indexes grid points in [0,chunk_size), and 'type' is atomKK->k_type (assigned at :190), whose extent is atom->nmax. The same kernel's ComputeNeigh counterpart hard-codes the grid-point type: :429-431 'const int itype = 1; int ielem = 0; if (chemflag) ielem = d_map[itype];', matching the CPU style src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:233-236. Same code in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h (TagCSNAGridLocalPreUi overloads).
failure_scenario: A 500-atom system with a 32x32x32 local grid gives chunk_size = 32768 >> atom->nmax, so type(iatom) reads far past the type array and d_map[itype] is then indexed with arbitrary garbage -> CUDA 'an illegal memory access was encountered' or silently wrong ielem; with 'chem' enabled the central element is wrong even when in bounds.
suggested_fix: Use the grid-point element consistently: 'const int ielem = chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0;' in all three TagCSNAGridPreUi overloads.

summary: max_neighs is hard-coded to 100 and the ComputeNeigh kernel writes snaKK.rij/wj/rcutij/inside at an unbounded offset, so a grid point with more than 100 atoms inside the cutoff overruns the SNA neighbour arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:195-196 '// max_neighs is defined here - think of more elaborate methods.\n  max_neighs = 100;' then :209 'snaKK.grow_rij(chunk_size, max_neighs, padding_factor);' while the neighbour loop at :458-487 does 'if (rsq < rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype) && rsq > 1e-20) { snaKK.rij(ii,offset,0) = ...; ... offset++; }' with no 'offset < max_neighs' guard. The CPU style sizes the buffers for every atom: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:220 'snaptr->grow_rij(ntotal);'. Same in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h.
failure_scenario: Any realistic SNAP cutoff (rcutfac*2*radelem ~ 5 A) around a grid point in a dense system holds several hundred atoms; offsets >= 100 write outside snaKK.rij -> device heap corruption, and even without the overrun ComputeCayleyKlein/ComputeUi only iterate jnbor < max_neighs so neighbours past 100 are dropped and the bispectrum is wrong.
suggested_fix: Compute the true maximum neighbour count per chunk (a parallel_reduce over d_ninside, as pair snap/kk does with its neighbour list) and call grow_rij with it, or at minimum clamp 'offset' and raise an error when ninside > max_neighs.

summary: k_cutsq is filled with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, so multi-type systems use the type-1 cutoff for all neighbours instead of the per-type cutoff the CPU style uses.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:66-73 'cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1];\n  for (int i = 1; i <= atom->ntypes; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= atom->ntypes; j++){ k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = k_cutsq.view_host()(j,i) = cutsq_tmp; ... } }' and the kernel test at :446 'if (rsq >= rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype) || rsq < 1e-20)' with itype fixed at 1. The CPU style selects neighbours with the j-type cutoff: src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:258 'if (rsq < cutsq[jtype][jtype] && rsq > 1e-20)', where cutsq[i][i] = (2*radelem[i]*rcutfac)^2 (:79-87). Same in src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h:65-72.
failure_scenario: A two-type SNAP descriptor with radelem 0.5 and 1.0: the /kk grid compute includes/excludes type-2 neighbours using the type-1 cutoff, producing bispectrum components that differ from 'compute sna/grid' on the same configuration.
suggested_fix: Copy the real cutsq matrix into k_cutsq ('k_cutsq.view_host()(i,j) = cutsq[i][j]') and test against rnd_cutsq(jtype,jtype) to match the CPU selection rule.

summary: The ComputeNeigh kernel omits the compute-group filter, so grid descriptors include atoms outside the compute's group.
failure_scenario: 'compute g sub sna/grid/kk grid ...' on a subgroup returns the same descriptors as a whole-system compute, silently including atoms the user excluded.
suggested_fix: Sync MASK_MASK, keep a mask view, and 'continue' on '!(mask(j) & groupbit)' in both neighbour loops.

summary: setup() allocates grid, gridall and gridlocal on every call without first deallocating, leaking the whole global grid on each run command.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:150-169 deliberately skips ComputeGrid::setup() (which begins with deallocate(), src/ML-SNAP/compute_grid.cpp:67-73) and then unconditionally does 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_grid, grid, ...); memory->create(gridall, ...); if (...) { gridlocal_allocated = 1; memory->create4d_offset(gridlocal, ...); }'. Modify::setup() calls compute[i]->setup() at the start of every run (src/modify.cpp:301), and Memory::create simply overwrites the pointer.
failure_scenario: A script with N 'run' commands leaks N-1 copies of grid + gridall (2 * nx*ny*nz * size_array_cols doubles) plus gridlocal; a 100x100x100 grid with 60 columns leaks ~1 GB per extra run.
suggested_fix: Call ComputeGrid::deallocate() (or free grid/gridall/gridlocal explicitly) at the top of the KOKKOS setup() before re-creating them.

summary: Neighbour weights, cutoffs and inner-cutoff parameters are looked up by element index while the CPU style looks them up by atom type, so they differ whenever the type-to-element map is not the identity (including every non-chem multi-type run).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:467-479 'int jelem = 0; if (chemflag) jelem = d_map[jtype]; ... snaKK.wj(ii,offset) = d_wjelem[jelem]; snaKK.rcutij(ii,offset) = (2.0*d_radelem[jelem])*rcutfac; ... snaKK.sinnerij(ii,offset) = 0.5*(d_sinnerelem[ielem] + d_sinnerelem[jelem]);' vs src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp:263-267 'snaptr->wj[ninside] = wjelem[jtype]; snaptr->rcutij[ninside] = 2.0 * radelem[jtype] * rcutfac; if (switchinnerflag) { snaptr->sinnerij[ninside] = sinnerelem[jelem]; snaptr->dinnerij[ninside] = dinnerelem[jelem]; }'. With chemflag off jelem is always 0, so every neighbour gets wjelem[1] and radelem[1]. The in-source comment at :472-473 records the uncertainty.
failure_scenario: Two atom types with radelem 0.5/1.0 and wjelem 1.0/0.96 and no 'chem' keyword: the /kk grid compute weights every neighbour as type 1, so its bispectrum differs from 'compute sna/grid'.
suggested_fix: Index d_wjelem/d_radelem by jtype (after sizing those views by ntypes, see the allocation finding) and use sinnerelem[jelem] without the 0.5 average, exactly as the CPU loop does.

summary: Leftover debug scaffolding: an <iostream> include (forbidden by the project style), an unused d_test view, and a deep_copy of a partly uninitialized h_map.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:39 '#include <iostream>'; :81 'MemKK::realloc_kokkos(d_test, "ComputeSNAGridKokkos::test", nelements);' with :92-93 'auto h_test = ...; h_test(0) = 2.0;' and :121 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_test,h_test);' -- d_test is never read; :90 'auto h_map = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_map);' leaves h_map(0) uninitialized before :119 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_map,h_map);'. Compare src/KOKKOS/compute_gaussian_grid_local_kokkos.cpp:74/86 for the same h_map issue.
failure_scenario: No wrong results, but <iostream> violates the LAMMPS I/O rules and the uninitialized copy trips memory sanitizers.
suggested_fix: Remove the iostream include and the d_test view; zero h_map (or skip the copy) when chemflag is off.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 04
summary: compute sna/grid/kk (and sna/grid/local/kk) fills k_cutsq with cutsq[1][1] for every type pair, sizes d_radelem/d_wjelem/d_sinnerelem/d_dinnerelem with nelements but fills ntypes entries (sinner/dinner at index i, not i-1), and its PreUi kernels look up type(iatom) with a grid-point index.
evidence: compute_sna_grid_kokkos_impl.h:66-73 (cutsq_tmp = cutsq[1][1] for all i,j), 76-103 (realloc with nelements, loop to atom->ntypes writing h_radelem(i-1) and h_sinnerelem(i)), 516-523 (int itype = type(iatom); ielem = d_map[itype]; with iatom in [0,chunk_size)). Same code in compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos_impl.h. CPU src/ML-SNAP/compute_sna_grid.cpp uses cutsq[jtype][jtype] and hard-codes the grid-point element.
failure_scenario: Multi-type SNAP grid on a GPU: heap overflow of the element mirrors when ntypes > nelements (the default nelements=1), wrong cutoff for all types but type 1, and an out-of-bounds/garbage element lookup whenever the grid chunk exceeds nmax -> wrong or crashing descriptor output.
suggested_fix: Size the element views by ntypes (or index by element consistently), copy the real cutsq table, and use the grid-point element (chemflag ? d_map[1] : 0) in PreUi as ComputeNeigh already does. Also address the unbounded max_neighs=100 and the missing group filter reported by group 04.

summary: FixNHKokkos::remap() drops the entire 'isochoric' branch of FixNH::remap(), so 'fix npt/kk ... isochoric <dims>' silently runs as an ordinary NPT and does not conserve the reference volume.
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all npt/kk temp 300 300 100 x 0 0 1000 isochoric yz' -- the y and z box lengths are never rescaled to keep the volume at vol_start, so the /kk run has a monotonically drifting volume and a completely different trajectory/pressure from the identical non-kk run, with no warning.
suggested_fix: Port the isochoric block from src/fix_nh.cpp:1236-1298 into FixNHKokkos::remap(), or (minimally) add 'if (isochoric) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot (yet) use isochoric with fix npt/kk");' in FixNHKokkos::init().

summary: nh_v_press() and nh_v_temp() call temperature->restore_bias_all() rather than restore_bias_all_kk() on a kokkosable temperature compute, forcing a full device->host copy of v twice per timestep.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.cpp:578-579 'if (which == BIAS) { if (temperature->kokkosable) temperature->restore_bias_all();' and the identical line at :733-734, while the matching remove calls at :558 and :716 correctly use remove_bias_all_kk().  Every KOKKOS temperature compute implements restore_bias_all() as 'restore_bias_all_kk(); atomKK->sync(Host,V_MASK);' (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_partial_kokkos.cpp:212-216, and the same shape in compute_temp_deform/ramp/com/profile/region_kokkos.cpp), i.e. the non-_kk entry point adds a host copy of the whole velocity array.  All sibling fixes use the _kk form: src/KOKKOS/fix_temp_rescale_kokkos.cpp:162, fix_temp_berendsen_kokkos.cpp:159, fix_nvt_sllod_kokkos.cpp:386, fix_langevin_kokkos.cpp:371.
failure_scenario: GPU run of 'fix 1 all npt/kk temp ... ' with 'fix_modify 1 temp <a temp/partial/kk or temp/profile/kk compute>': every timestep transfers atom->v device->host twice (once from nh_v_press, once from nh_v_temp) for no reason; results are correct but the port loses most of its speedup.
suggested_fix: Change both kokkosable branches to temperature->restore_bias_all_kk().

summary: FixNHKokkos::remap() converts the dilate-group atoms with a host loop (two full x host/device round trips per remap) although DomainKokkos already provides a device x2lamda/lamda2x variant that takes a groupbit.
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all npt/kk ... dilate mygroup' on a GPU: remap() is called twice per timestep and each call copies the whole coordinate array device->host and back twice, so the /kk barostat is slower than the plain CPU one; results are correct.
suggested_fix: Replace both host loops with 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal, dilate_group_bit);' and 'domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal, dilate_group_bit);'.

summary: FixNHKokkos::remap() overrides FixNH::remap() but drops the whole isochoric branch, so 'fix npt/kk ... isochoric' silently runs as ordinary NPT and does not conserve the reference volume.
verified_by: orchestrator (remap override at src/KOKKOS/fix_nh_kokkos.h:66 / .cpp:354; grep 'isochoric' over fix_nh_kokkos.cpp returns nothing, while FixNH::remap in src/fix_nh.cpp has isofac/isochoric logic in five places).

summary: The second-group filter (mask[j] & jgroupbit) is applied only in the single-column template branch, so multi-column 'compute coord/atom cutoff R group <g2> t1 t2 ...' counts neighbours from every group instead of only group2.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_coord_atom_kokkos.cpp:279-280 'if (NCOL == 1)\n        if (!(mask[j] & jgroupbit)) continue;' -- the guard is compiled out for the ncol>1 instantiation TagComputeCoordAtom<CUTOFF,0> launched at :236. The CPU base applies it in BOTH branches: src/compute_coord_atom.cpp:233 'if (mask[j] & jgroupbit) {' (ncol==1) and src/compute_coord_atom.cpp:265 'if (mask[j] & jgroupbit) {' (ncol>1 branch, lines 249-278).
failure_scenario: 'group sub type 1' then 'compute c1 all coord/atom/kk cutoff 3.0 group sub 1 2' gives per-type coordination numbers that include neighbours outside group 'sub'; the non-KOKKOS compute coord/atom returns smaller, correct numbers for the same input.
suggested_fix: Move the jgroupbit test out of the 'if (NCOL == 1)' guard so it runs for every CSTYLE==CUTOFF instantiation (the ORIENT path uses jgroupbit = 'all', so an unconditional test is still equivalent to the CPU ORIENT loop).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 04, line corrected)
summary: The second-group filter (mask[j] & jgroupbit) is applied only when NCOL == 1, so multi-column 'compute coord/atom cutoff R group G t1 t2 ...' counts neighbors from every group.
evidence: compute_coord_atom_kokkos.cpp:202-203 'if (NCOL == 1) if (!(mask[j] & jgroupbit)) continue;'; src/compute_coord_atom.cpp applies the jgroupbit test in both the ncol==1 and ncol>1 branches.
failure_scenario: compute coord/atom/kk with a group keyword and per-type columns returns coordination numbers that include atoms outside the group.
suggested_fix: Apply the jgroupbit test unconditionally in the CUTOFF path.

summary: In the setup path (setup_pre_force -> solve_reactions(vflag,false)) the KOKKOS version initializes the "Old" species concentrations only for atoms in the fix group, whereas the CPU FixRX initializes them for every local atom.
failure_scenario: `fix rx` applied to a subset group (e.g. `group mobile ...; fix 1 mobile rx ...`).  On the setup step the *Old per-atom properties of atoms outside `mobile` stay at their fix property/atom default (0.0) under /kk, while the CPU run sets them equal to the current concentrations.  Downstream consumers of the Old values (fix eos/table/rx, pair dpd/fdt/energy) then see a spurious concentration change for those atoms and the /kk run diverges from the CPU run.
suggested_fix: Add a separate parallel_for over all nlocal atoms (no groupbit test) that copies d_dvector(atom_ind,i) into d_dvector(atom_ind_old,i) in the setup (ZERO_RATES) path, mirroring fix_rx.cpp:551-558.

summary: Dead host-only copies of the ODE solver (rk4, rkf45, rkf45_step, rkf45_h0, rhs, rhs_dense, rhs_sparse) are never called and would dereference device views from host code if they ever were.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:174 (rk4), :587 (rkf45_step), :690 (rkf45_h0), :775 (rkf45), :875 (rhs), :887 (rhs_dense), :921 (rhs_sparse) are plain host member functions.  A grep of the file shows they are only called by each other; the only solver actually used is k_rk4/k_rkf45 from the device kernel (fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1304 and :1308).  rhs_dense reads `d_kineticsData.stoichReactants(jrxn,ispecies)` (line 903) and rhs_sparse reads `this->d_kineticsData.nuk/nu/inu` (lines 931-935) -- these are `ArrayTypes<DeviceType>` views, i.e. GPU memory for the /kk/device instantiation.
failure_scenario: No failure today (dead code), but ~350 lines of unmaintained duplicate solver that segfaults on a GPU build the moment anyone wires it up, and that silently diverges from the device solver if only one of the two copies is fixed.
suggested_fix: Delete the host-only rk4/rkf45/rkf45_step/rkf45_h0/rhs/rhs_dense/rhs_sparse members (and their declarations in fix_rx_kokkos.h:156-188), keeping only the k_* device versions.

summary: Two large `#if 0` blocks hold disabled alternative lambda implementations of the two temperature kernels, plus commented-out member declarations in the header.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1828-1894 (`#if 0` ... `#else` ... `#endif` around a LAMMPS_LAMBDA copy of Tag_FixRxKokkos_firstPairOperator) and :1908-1931 (same for the 2nd pair operator); src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1439 (`//DAT::tdual_int_scalar k_error_flag("pair:error_flag");`), :1199-1219 (`//else {` ... `//}`); src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.h:225-226, :257, :267 commented-out member declarations.  The project code-review rule states that disabled/alternative implementations must be removed entirely.
failure_scenario: Maintenance hazard only: the disabled copies already differ from the live kernels (e.g. the #if 0 copy at line 1877 omits the `NEIGHFLAG==HALF||NEIGHFLAG==HALFTHREAD` guard that the live kernel has at line 1728), so a future reader can be misled into reinstating a wrong version.
suggested_fix: Delete the `#if 0` blocks and the commented-out declarations.

summary: Device kernels call unqualified C library math (pow, exp, sqrt, fabs, fmax, fmin) instead of the Kokkos:: equivalents required by the KOKKOS package rules, inconsistently with line 1093 which does use Kokkos::pow.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1284-1286 inside operator()(Tag_FixRxKokkos_solveSystems...):
        userData.kFor[irxn] = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(static_cast<double>(d_kineticsData.Arr(irxn)) *
                               pow(theta, static_cast<double>(d_kineticsData.nArr(irxn))) *
                               exp(-static_cast<double>(d_kineticsData.Ea(irxn)) / boltz / theta));
and in the KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION helpers: :1040 `pow(...)`, :397/:437/:446/:467-468 (`sqrt`, `fmax`, `fmin`), :509/:520/:524/:536-547 (`fabs`, `sqrt`, `fmax`, `fmin`), :1717-1718 (`sqrt`).  Compare src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1093 which correctly uses `Kokkos::pow`.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos:: math in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Compiles today on CUDA/HIP because ::pow/::exp/::sqrt are provided as device functions, but breaks on backends/toolchains where only the Kokkos:: wrappers are guaranteed, and blocks a future switch of these accumulators to KK_FLOAT.
suggested_fix: Replace the unqualified calls in all KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION bodies with Kokkos::pow/exp/sqrt/fabs/fmax/fmin.

summary: FixRxKokkos::odeDiagnostics reads the host mirror of atom->mask without syncing MASK_MASK to the host.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_rx_kokkos.cpp:1583 `HAT::t_int_1d h_mask = atomKK->k_mask.view_host();` and line 1592 `if (h_mask(j) & groupbit) {`, with no `atomKK->sync(Host,MASK_MASK)` anywhere in odeDiagnostics (the function spans lines 1505-1662).  FixRxKokkos declares `datamask_read = EMPTY_MASK` so ModifyKokkos does not sync anything for it either; every other host-side read in this file is preceded by an explicit sync.
failure_scenario: GPU run where the group mask was last written on the device (e.g. `group ... dynamic` handled by a KOKKOS fix, or a device-side border/exchange): the ODE diagnostics loop selects the wrong atoms, so the reported per-group ODE step/function-call statistics are wrong.  Diagnostics only, no effect on the trajectory.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->sync(Host,MASK_MASK);` before line 1583.

summary: ModifyKokkos::energy_atom() is a byte-for-byte copy of Modify::energy_atom(), adding no KOKKOS sync/modify handling, so the override serves no purpose.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp:504-514 and src/modify.cpp:514-524 have identical bodies ('eatom = fix[list_energy_atom[i]]->eatom; if (!eatom) continue; for (j = 0; j < nlocal; j++) energy[j] += eatom[j];'). Unlike every other wrapper in modify_kokkos.cpp it contains no atomKK->sync/modified and no auto_sync bracket. (This is currently harmless because no fix in src/KOKKOS sets energy_peratom_flag, so list_energy_atom only ever holds non-KOKKOS fixes whose eatom is plain host memory.)
failure_scenario: None today; but the empty override hides the fact that the first KOKKOS fix to provide a device-resident per-atom energy would be read here without a sync.
suggested_fix: Delete the override and let Modify::energy_atom() be used, or make it actually sync the fix's per-atom energy when the fix is kokkosable.

summary: ModifyKokkos::post_run() is the only fix-calling wrapper that omits the auto_sync bracketing used around every other non-KOKKOS fix callback.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/modify_kokkos.cpp:522-528: 'for (int i = 0; i < nfix; i++) { atomKK->sync(fix[i]->execution_space, fix[i]->datamask_read); fix[i]->post_run(); atomKK->modified(fix[i]->execution_space, fix[i]->datamask_modify); }'. Every other wrapper in the file (e.g. end_of_step at :446-449, post_force at :379-382, min_post_force at :745-748, and energy_couple/energy_global as of commit 9ba00b501) wraps the call as 'int prev_auto_sync = lmp->kokkos->auto_sync; if (!fix[...]->kokkosable) lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1; fix[...]->hook(); lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = prev_auto_sync;'. The purpose (documented in src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:425-428) is that a non-KOKKOS style running inside a KOKKOS run needs auto_sync on so that any sync()/modified() it triggers indirectly (e.g. through the DomainKokkos x2lamda/lamda2x overrides) writes through to the legacy host arrays it reads.
failure_scenario: A non-KOKKOS fix whose post_run() goes through a KOKKOS-overridden helper that syncs to the device (DomainKokkos::x2lamda/lamda2x, AtomKokkos::sort) leaves the legacy host arrays behind, so anything the fix reads afterwards in post_run() (or a later 'run' command that re-reads them) sees stale coordinates.
suggested_fix: Add the same 'prev_auto_sync' save/force/restore around 'fix[i]->post_run();' that all the other ModifyKokkos wrappers use.

summary: Every non-KOKKOS compute keeps Compute's default datamask_modify = ALL_MASK (compute.cpp:98), so each setup() marks every per-atom array host-modified and forces a full host->device upload on the next device consumer even though Compute::setup() is read-only for essentially all computes.
evidence: modify_kokkos.cpp:60-67; compute.cpp:97-98 datamask_read = datamask_modify = ALL_MASK; compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.cpp:41-47 documents the same cost (issue #5080) and works around it only for that one compute.
failure_scenario: Any -k on g 1 run with one plain (non-/kk) compute defined: at every run setup, one extra full transform+upload of x/v/f/tag/type/mask/image/... after the setup loop. Correct results, wasted transfer.
suggested_fix: For !kokkosable computes, sync for datamask_read but skip the modified() claim (or claim EMPTY_MASK), matching what setup() actually writes.

summary: Same d_flag race as bond_fene_kokkos: plain stores of 2 (fatal) and 1 (warning) to one shared scalar can hide a 'Bad FENE bond' abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_nm_kokkos.cpp:174-180 'if (rlogarg < 0.02) { if (rlogarg <= -0.21) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.02; }' and :121-124 'if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(...); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");'. CPU base src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/bond_fene_nm.cpp:86-91 aborts per-bond with 'if (rlogarg <= -.21) error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond");'.
failure_scenario: Concurrent bonds with rlogarg <= -0.21 and -0.21 < rlogarg < 0.02: the fatal marker can be lost and the run continues instead of aborting.
suggested_fix: Use Kokkos::atomic_max(&d_flag(), ...) instead of plain assignment.

summary: pair zbl/kk scales the ZBL force and energy by special_lj[sbmask(j)], while the CPU pair zbl (and the /omp and /gpu variants) deliberately ignore the special-bond factors, so the /kk variant gives different forces/energies for 1-2, 1-3 and 1-4 pairs that remain in the neighbor list.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_zbl_kokkos.cpp:148-151 fills `special_lj[0..3] = force->special_lj[...]`, and the generic driver applies it: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:156-166 `const KK_FLOAT factor_lj = c.special_lj[sbmask(j)]; j &= NEIGHMASK; ... const KK_FLOAT fpair = factor_lj*c.template compute_fpair<...>(rsq,i,j,itype,jtype);` and :181 `evdwl = factor_lj * c.template compute_evdwl<...>(...)`.  The CPU base src/pair_zbl.cpp:105-144 does `j = jlist[jj]; j &= NEIGHMASK;` and never reads force->special_lj -- `grep -n 'special_lj\|factor_lj' src/pair_zbl.cpp` returns nothing; the same is true of src/OPENMP/pair_zbl_omp.cpp:114 and lib/gpu/lal_zbl.cu.
failure_scenario: A molecular system with a kspace solver (Neighbor::init then forces special_flag[1..3]=2, so 1-2/1-3/1-4 pairs stay in the list carrying their sbmask bits) and `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5`: pair zbl computes the full ZBL repulsion on those pairs, pair zbl/kk multiplies it by 0.0/0.0/0.5, so CPU and KOKKOS runs of the same input give different forces and energies.
suggested_fix: Decide which behaviour is intended and make the two agree: either set `special_lj[1..3] = 1.0` in PairZBLKokkos::compute() to match the CPU style, or add the factor_lj handling to pair_zbl.cpp/pair_zbl_omp.cpp/lib/gpu and document the change.

summary: improper sqdistharm/kk drops the six domain->minimum_image() calls the CPU ImproperSQDistHarm::compute applies to its bond vectors, diverging from the base style when a bond vector exceeds half the box.
evidence: CPU src/YAFF/improper_sqdistharm.cpp:98-131 folds every difference vector (`xab = x[i2][0] - x[i1][0]; ... domain->minimum_image(FLERR, xab,yab,zab);` and the same for xac, xad, xbc, xbd, xcd). The KOKKOS kernel src/KOKKOS/improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp:149-167 forms the identical differences with no folding; `grep -n minimum_image src/KOKKOS/improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp` is empty and domain.h is not included. The rest of the kernel (:169-207: xna/yna/zna, rna, da, da2, eimproper = k*(da2-chi)^2, a = 4*da*k*(da2-chi), f1..f4) matches CPU :133-169 exactly, and a diff of improper_sqdistharm_kokkos.cpp against improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp differs only in those three energy/force lines, so the whole family shares the omission.
failure_scenario: improper_style sqdistharm vs sqdistharm/kk in a periodic cell whose shortest edge is under twice an improper bond length: CPU folds the vectors before building the plane normal and projection, /kk does not, so energies and all four forces differ.
suggested_fix: Add the device-side minimum_image used by src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:243-295 (with domain->triclinic/xprd/*_half copied into the functor in compute()) and apply it to the six difference vectors.

summary: The energy is rebuilt as cos(theta)cos(theta0)+sin(theta)sin(theta0) using the SMALL-clamped sine, so it differs from the base class's exact cos(theta-theta0) for near-collinear angles.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_cosine_delta_kokkos.cpp:189-201: `KK_FLOAT s = Kokkos::sqrt(1.0 - c*c);` / `if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL;` / `const KK_FLOAT cot = c/s;` / ... / `const KK_FLOAT dcostheta = c*c0 + s*s0;` / `const KK_FLOAT tk = d_k[type] * (1.0 - dcostheta);` / `if (eflag) eangle = tk;`. The CPU base clamps s only for the cot term and computes the energy from the unclamped angle: src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/angle_cosine_delta.cpp:87-98: `theta = acos(c);` / `s = sqrt(1.0 - c*c); if (s < SMALL) s = SMALL; cot = c/s;` / `dtheta = theta - theta0[type]; dcostheta = cos(dtheta); tk = k[type] * (1.0-dcostheta);`. SMALL is 0.001 in both (kokkos line 34, base line 35). The force terms a11/a12/a22/b11/b12/b22 are identical, so only the energy diverges.
failure_scenario: angle_style cosine/delta/kk with an angle within ~0.06 deg of 0 or 180 degrees: the /kk energy is off by k*(0.001 - sin(theta))*sin(theta0), i.e. up to 1e-3*k per angle, versus the CPU value. Shows up as a small but systematic energy mismatch in force-style regression tests for collapsed/linear angles.
suggested_fix: Compute the energy from the unclamped sine (keep a separate clamped copy for cot), or use Kokkos::cos(Kokkos::acos(c) - theta0) as the base does.

summary: MinKokkos re-declares the iterate() return-code enum, hiding Min's identical enum in every KOKKOS min style, but omits MAXVDOTF -- so the values only agree by accident and MinFireKokkos silently falls through to the base enumerator.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.h:42-44 '// possible return values of iterate() method\n  enum{MAXITER,MAXEVAL,ETOL,FTOL,DOWNHILL,ZEROALPHA,ZEROFORCE,\n       ZEROQUAD,TRSMALL,INTERROR,TIMEOUT};' versus src/min.h:60-74 which declares the same eleven names plus 'MAXVDOTF'.  src/KOKKOS/min_fire_kokkos.cpp:234 'if (max_vdotf_negatif > 0 && vdotf_negatif > max_vdotf_negatif) return MAXVDOTF;' resolves through the derived enum to Min::MAXVDOTF only because MinKokkos has no member of that name.  The codes are consumed positionally by src/min.cpp:1024-1038 'char *Min::stopstrings(int n) { const char *strings[] = {...}; return (char *) strings[n]; }'.
failure_scenario: No wrong behavior today (the eleven shared enumerators happen to be in the same order). If anyone inserts or reorders an entry in Min's enum, the KOKKOS min styles keep the old numbering and Min::run() prints the wrong stop reason, or indexes stopstrings() out of range.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate enum from min_kokkos.h and use the inherited Min enum.

summary: The region /kk device kernels call unqualified sqrt()/sin()/cos() instead of the Kokkos:: math functions the package rules require for device code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/region_block_kokkos.h:273 `contact[n].r = sqrt(delx * delx + dely * dely + delz * delz);` and :319-320 `double sine = sin(angle); double cosine = cos(angle);` inside KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION members; the same appears in region_cone_kokkos.h:85,91,97,122,123, region_cylinder_kokkos.h:85,90,95,119,120, region_ellipsoid_kokkos.h:121,122, region_plane_kokkos.h:104,105, region_prism_kokkos.h:106,107 and region_sphere_kokkos.h:131,155,179,193,229,230.  .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: "Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...)"; the dihedral kernels reviewed alongside these files all use Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos.
failure_scenario: Compiles today on the CUDA/HIP backends (the global ::sqrt has device overloads there), but it is the documented portability hazard for other backends and is inconsistent with the rest of the package.
suggested_fix: Replace the unqualified sqrt/sin/cos calls in the seven region_*_kokkos.h device functions with Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::sin / Kokkos::cos.

summary: The 'Overlapping small/large' and 'Overlapping large/large' fatal checks of the CPU style are dropped, so overlapping colloids silently produce Inf/NaN forces instead of aborting.
evidence: src/COLLOID/pair_colloid.cpp:151-152 'if (rsq <= K[1]) error->one(FLERR,"Overlapping small/large in pair colloid");' and :190-191 'if (r <= K[1]) error->one(FLERR,"Overlapping large/large in pair colloid");'. src/KOKKOS/pair_colloid_kokkos.cpp:159-208 (compute_fpair SMALL_LARGE/LARGE_LARGE branches) contain no equivalent check; K3/K0 go to zero and the result is Inf/NaN.
failure_scenario: pair_style colloid/kk with two large colloids that come into contact: the CPU run stops with a clear error, the /kk run keeps integrating NaN forces and silently corrupts the trajectory.
suggested_fix: Accumulate an overlap flag in the kernel (e.g. a device scalar reduced with the EV_FLOAT or a separate parallel_reduce) and call error->one() on the host after the kernel, as other KOKKOS styles do for kernel-detected errors.

summary: The include guard of compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.h is named after a different, renamed-away style (LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_BONDS_KOKKOS_H), and pair_reaxff_kokkos.h still carries the pre-rename LMP_PAIR_REAXC_KOKKOS_H guard.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/compute_reaxff_atom_kokkos.h:26-27:
  #ifndef LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_BONDS_KOKKOS_H
  #define LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_BONDS_KOKKOS_H
whereas the CPU parent src/REAXFF/compute_reaxff_atom.h:24-25 correctly uses
  #ifndef LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_ATOM_H
  #define LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_ATOM_H
and src/KOKKOS/pair_reaxff_kokkos.h:23:
  #ifndef LMP_PAIR_REAXC_KOKKOS_H
while the CPU parent src/REAXFF/pair_reaxff.h:31 uses LMP_PAIR_REAXFF_H ('reax/c' was renamed to 'reaxff').
A scan of every .h in src/ (progress_rules_D/rule6b.py plus a tree-wide duplicate scan) finds NO duplicate guard macro today, so nothing is currently miscompiled.  (The other name deviations found -- fftdata_kokkos.h:17 LMP_FFT_DATA_KOKKOS_H, fix_addforce_kokkos.h:23 LMP_FIX_ADD_FORCE_KOKKOS_H, fix_dpd_energy_kokkos.h:23 LMP_FIX_DPDE_KOKKOS_H, kokkos_type.h:15 LMP_LMPTYPE_KOKKOS_H, meam_kokkos.h:14 LMP_MEAMKOKKOS_H, min_linesearch_kokkos.h:15 LMP_MIN_LSRCH_KOKKOS_H -- mostly mirror the CPU header's own guard name and are benign.)
failure_scenario: If a compute_reaxff_bonds_kokkos.h is ever re-added under its historical name (it existed before the reaxff rename) and both headers end up in one translation unit, the second one is silently skipped and its class is undefined; the wrong names also defeat grep-based tooling that maps guard macros to files.
suggested_fix: Rename the guards to LMP_COMPUTE_REAXFF_ATOM_KOKKOS_H and LMP_PAIR_REAXFF_KOKKOS_H.
